_about: Hand-reviewed filing for tools/fetch_trials.py. Keys are NCT IDs. q = A-F, APPROVED or OTHER. note = one plain line on what the trial tests and which question it could help answer (from the registry record, not from outside knowledge). rank orders the Other section (lower = more relevant; only the first 25 are shown). exclude = true removes a study that passed the automatic filters, with a reason. A trial not listed here goes to Other as 'not yet reviewed'. Reviewed 11/03/2026.

_section_notes.A: Trials whose intervention targets Epstein-Barr virus (EBV), such as antivirals or EBV-targeted cells. mRNA-1195 (NCT06735248) is listed here provisionally: its registry entry enrolls only EBV-positive people but does not name the vaccine's target, so its place in this section needs a primary source.
_section_notes.B: Trials in progressive MS or on smoldering (chronic active) lesions such as paramagnetic rim lesions and slowly expanding lesions. Their main outcomes vary: disability worsening, MRI or PET measures, and in some cases safety or fatigue, so check each record. None of them uses PIRA itself as the main outcome.
_section_notes.C: Trials whose stated aim or main outcome is myelin repair or nerve protection: nerve-signal speed (evoked potentials), vision after optic neuritis, brain shrinkage, or walking in progressive MS with a drug aimed at nerve protection.
_section_notes.D: Autologous (and one allogeneic) stem cell transplant trials, and CAR-T and other gene-engineered T-cell trials. Phase 1 trials are included here because they are cell therapies. Most CAR-T trials are small, single-arm and measure safety first.
_section_notes.E: No active phase 2 or 3 trial in this run uses a blood biomarker such as sNfL or GFAP to decide treatment, and none has one as its main outcome. Biomarker-guided trials in earlier phases (for example NCT03109288, TRAP-MS, phase 1/2) fall outside the query's phase filter.
_section_notes.F: No active interventional trial in the query results tests why MS clusters. That question is mostly answered by family, cohort and registry studies, which are observational and outside this query.
_section_notes.APPROVED: Studies of drugs already approved or widely used for MS: new doses, new forms (such as under-the-skin injection), children, head-to-head comparisons, biosimilars, long-term extensions, and stopping or stepping down treatment.
_section_notes.OTHER: Trials that do not clearly fit one lab question. New drugs for relapsing MS and cell therapies other than stem cell transplant and CAR-T come first; symptom, rehabilitation and imaging studies follow.
